extra.abstract_end: and drove back to within 0.2\,m of its start without any operator intervention
extra.setup: The robot was placed in a carpeted hallway of a furnished apartment at night with the room lights on, the exploration service was started from the PC and Explore was pressed once; nobody touched the robot or the keyboard afterwards. Doors stood as they were left; there are no stairs on this floor.
extra.discussion: Mapped area grows fastest in the first two minutes, when every goal opens a new room to the 360\textdegree{} lidar, and creeps up afterwards as the robot visits the corners and gaps behind furniture one at a time; the number of open frontiers peaks at about four and a half minutes and falls to zero after 11.6 minutes, when the robot returned to its start. The single failure was a goal on the far side of a wall that the planner could reach only through unknown space; the controller made progress but not enough, and the goal was dropped after its timeout of 156\,s. The mean speed over the run, 0.098\,m/s, is close to the controller's cruise speed of 0.10\,m/s, so the time was spent driving rather than waiting or recovering. The long white streak at the top of the map is free space seen along a few rays through a narrow gap (most likely a door left ajar); the frontier at its end is a ray or two wide, below the 0.30\,m minimum frontier length, so the explorer ignored it, which is also why the room behind it is missing from the map.

end_note: No frontier left after 11.6 min: drove back, stopped 0.2 m from the start, saved the map. Zero operator interventions.
takeaway: Pressed Explore once; the robot chose all 30 goals itself and came home.
notes_map: ~60 s. One unattended run in an apartment: 47 square metres in twelve and a half minutes, 74 metres driven, 30 goals chosen by the robot, one failed, behind a wall. When nothing was left it drove home and saved the map. The streak at the top is free space seen through a narrow gap; too narrow to count as a frontier.
notes_progress: ~45 s. Area grows fastest in the first two minutes, when each goal opens a new room, then creeps up as corners are visited one by one. Frontiers peak around four minutes and reach zero at eleven and a half. The Pi used about one and a half cores.
